Recommend **publish-verified-testimony**.

It best advances the Series commitment to contested history by placing **monastery testimony preserved** back into public memory against **council archive position: retracted admission**. Authentication lets the testimony challenge official history credibly, while publication of verified copies leaves the originals secured under **archive protection: treaty protected**, preserving the archive as the **only evidentiary chain**. It also builds directly on **archive founding record: forged** without exposing the archive’s strongest records prematurely.

The principal tradeoff is delay: authentication slows public release, giving the council’s retracted position more time to shape public memory.

Deliberately excluded as irrelevant to this choice: **archive lantern condition: repaired**, the circumstances of its breaking and repair, and new investigation of the falsifier’s identity. Those facts do not determine how testimony should be made public while protecting the evidentiary chain.

This recommendation is non-authoritative and creates no canon, Book Direction, or Canonical State.
